t: That paragraph 4 of part VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 1 (a), as amended, is amended by striking out “(including apprenticeship and refresher or retraining training)” and by inserting in lieu thereof “(including apprenticeship, refresher or retraining and institutional on-farm training)”.

fable.w: The section is a purely textual amendment that adds institutional on-farm training to the kinds of training listed in a veterans regulation. The tempting reading is that the reference to a "Veterans Regulation" signals rulemaking, but Congress is directly amending the text itself and gives no agency authority to issue rules. Nothing here provides for comment, hearing, consultation, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: by inserting in lieu thereof “(including apprenticeship, refresher or retraining and institutional on-farm training)”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a regulation regarding the types of training covered. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. It simply changes the text of an existing rule.
qwen_block.s: That paragraph 4 of part VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 1 (a), as amended, is amended by striking out “(including apprenticeship and refresher or retraining training)” and by inserting in lieu thereof “(including apprenticeship, refresher or retraining and institutional on-farm training)”.

opus.w: This section is a wording change that adds institutional on-farm training to the kinds of veterans' training covered. No one outside the federal government is consulted before any federal decision. The word "Regulation" might suggest rulemaking, but Congress is rewriting the text directly, not authorizing or requiring an agency to make rules. Also, veterans getting training benefits would be an application for benefits, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: is amended by striking out “(including apprenticeship and refresher or retraining training)” and by inserting in lieu thereof “(including apprenticeship, refresher or retraining and institutional on-farm training)”
opus.b: I'm calling this "No". The tempting reading is "Yes", because the section amends a "Veterans Regulation", and the examples treat authority to issue regulations as participation. That reading fails because this is Congress directly changing the wording of an existing regulation. It doesn't give an agency new rulemaking authority, and it doesn't set up a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a veterans' regulation regarding the types of training covered. It does not establish a process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The definition of participation excludes applications for benefits, and this text merely defines eligibility criteria within a regulation without requiring external input in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: That paragraph 4 of part VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 1 (a), as amended, is amended by striking out “(including apprenticeship and refresher or retraining training)” and by inserting in lieu thereof “(including apprenticeship, refresher or retraining and institutional on-farm training)”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the definition of eligible training implies a change in who can participate in benefits, but the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants from being considered "participation." Furthermore, this is a technical amendment to a regulation's text, not a procedural requirement for public input or consultation.
